_comment: POSTGRES, NO CONTAINERS — each worktree gets its own copy of the database;
the app is run directly (uvicorn/gunicorn/manage.py) on the assigned port.
This is quarterback's own shape; see the repo root .worktree.json.
Choose this over the docker template when your compose file is tracked in
git: the Docker path WRITES a generated docker-compose.yml into the worktree,
which would leave every worktree dirty and invite committing it.
PREREQUISITE: a .env in the main checkout holding url_env (DATABASE_URL).
create-worktree copies that file into the worktree and rewrites the database
name in it. No .env, no isolation — it cannot invent your credentials.
container 'auto' resolves whichever running Postgres answers as the URL's
user, so it survives being cloned into a differently-named directory. Pin a
name instead if several of your stacks share one username.
Then make your TEST SUITE honour that .env — see conftest-db-isolation.py
here. A suite that hardcodes its database URL will cheerfully rebuild the
shared one while the isolated copy sits unused.
